# park — leave enough context to resume

Save the session's stopping point while its reasons are still available. Summoned,
not automatic: no end-of-turn or context-percentage trigger.

Before reading or writing the handoff, read `references/session-handoff.md` for its
location, five fields, and evidence rules. This bundled reference is shared with
shape-catchup; neither skill depends on the other being installed.

## Write the handoff

1. Read the existing note, if present, and reconcile the live session with current
   files, git status, and the project's plan. Preserve still-relevant unresolved
   work and reasons when replacing an earlier note. Record rejected approaches
   explicitly so the next session does not revive them as unfinished work.
2. Draft the five fields with enough **what, why, and how far** to resume. Prefer
   decision-level prose; include a concrete file or command when it makes the next
   action executable, not an inventory of every changed file. Label inferred or
   unrecorded reasons instead of inventing them.
3. Show the exact content or diff before overwriting. Honor explicit authorization
   already given to save this handoff; otherwise obtain it. If the existing note
   has unrelated live work that cannot safely be carried forward, resolve that
   conflict with the user rather than discard it. Re-read `git rev-parse HEAD`
   at write time; record the date, or say that no git SHA is available.
4. Overwrite the selected note, report its location, and stop. No dated chain,
   commit, context clearing, or automatic next-skill invocation.

shape-catchup reconstructs the picture on return. shape-align owns durable project
priorities; roadmap work that outlives this session belongs on the board, not only
in this note.
